model: Specialty lender levered FCFE at cost of equity (engine route)

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment (Note 25)' RMB'000 3,885 (2473.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:7325); EquityAwardTaxes nil in every period; H1 FY2026 charge RMB 0.4m (pre-IPO options fully vested)
inputs.fx_note: CNY->HKD 1.1724, Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T22:01Z; cross-check 1/HKDCNY=X 0.8505 = 1.1758 (different timestamp, 0.3% apart). No dual listing to parity-check. All flows and per-share values are built in RMB and converted at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are HKD to match current_price, *_cny twins are the model currency.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday); not after-hours. 52-week range 0.32-15.96: the stock fell from HK$13.81 to HK$2.04 in the week of 2026-02-01 on 2.4bn shares and has drifted down since; the April/May 2026 top-up subscriptions were struck at HK$0.98 and HK$0.82, so the quote is real, not frozen
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,856.25m shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (1,546.875m + 2 x 154.6875m top-up subscription shares, H1 FY2026 interim report) plus 67.2189m vested pre-IPO share options at HK$0.183 (interim report share-option note), which are in the money at the current price and expire October 2028 = 1,923.47m fully diluted. Exercise proceeds (HK$12.3m = RMB 10.5m) are added in equity_bridge. The 1,716.4m 'diluted weighted average' in core_metrics is a period average that predates the second subscription and understates the live count by ~11%. Count held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The two 2026 placings were genuine non-SBC issuance and are already in the 1,856.25m; further controller-led top-up placings at distressed prices are a live risk named in the bear narrative, not modelled as a share-growth path.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 13.0% built in RMB: China 10-year CGB ~1.8% + 6.5% China ERP x levered beta ~1.4 (D/E 2.3x, 17-18% lending yields to lower-tier-city retail borrowers) = ~10.9%, plus ~2pp size/liquidity/governance premium (HK$0.6bn market cap, 97% drawdown, controller-driven placings). House precedents for large Chinese banks are 10.5-11.0% (0998.HK, 2016.HK); this is a sub-scale, short-term-secured-funded lessor. Same rate in all three scenarios - cyclicality and credit risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): office lease liabilities (RMB 10.5m at 30 June 2026) are excluded from debt (debt is zero in this model anyway) and the lease cash cost is charged in the flows - the interest is already inside pre-tax profit (the EBITDA margin here is post-finance-cost) and the principal (RMB 7.9m FY2025, 0.42% of revenue) is inside capex_pct on top of D&A. Rental-fleet vehicles are owned PP&E, not leases.
inputs.nci_treatment: Nil at 30 June 2026: the remaining 51% of Fujian Xidun (RMB 51.0m, May 2026) and 49% of Fujian ZyooCar (RMB 6.4m) were bought out in H1 FY2026, interim balance sheet shows NCI '-' (2473.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:2079). Flows are 100% attributable; no bridge deduction.
inputs.fcfe_mapping_note: Engine mapping for a levered FCFE: ebitda_margin_path = (pre-tax profit + D&A + SBC) / revenue, i.e. EBITDA AFTER net finance cost, so the engine's EBIT is pre-tax profit and the 25% cash tax applies to it; da_pct = depreciation incl. rental-fleet and ROU depreciation (FY2025 8.2%, H1 FY2026 12.0% after the Xidun fleet consolidated - 10.5% forward); capex_pct = da_pct + lease principal = maintenance of the fleet only; wc_capture_pct = -60 charges the equity-funded share of growth in net operating assets (equity / revenue 0.61 = 1,130.7 / TTM 1,854.6 at 30 June 2026, equivalently 34% equity share x 1.78 NOA/revenue at the 65.7% gearing), so growth consumes equity and run-off releases it at constant gearing. FY0 reference: FY2025 NI RMB 45.9m is the zero-growth FCFE; the actual FY2025 FCFE was ~RMB -130m because NOA grew RMB 526m. H1 FY2026 flows overlap the 30 June 2026 balance sheet by six months; immaterial with net_debt = 0 and no dividend.
inputs.notes: MODEL: levered FCFE capitalised at the cost of equity, run through the Drivers engine with net_debt = 0 (same route as 1186.HK). XXF is a finance-lease lender (net finance lease receivables RMB 1,840m, 31,508 contracts, 18.1% average yield) with a rental/e-hailing fleet and a thin-margin car-export arm; RMB 2,593m of secured bank, finance-leasing and supply-chain borrowings fund that book and are operating funding, like a bank's deposits, not net debt to subtract from an enterprise value. Reported owner FCF is structurally negative (FY2025 -534m) because lease-receivable growth sits in operating cash flow, and the unlevered alternative (EV ~RMB 2.2bn vs net debt RMB 2,167m) flips sign on half a point of WACC - meaningless. last_fcf / reported_fcf are kept on the contract's unlevered owner-FCF definition for auditability only; the engine builds the FCFE from components. A liquidation reference: book equity RMB 1,130.7m = HK$0.69/share fully diluted, 2.2x the price - but the controller is growing the book (two 2026 placings to buy vehicles), not running it off, and a 3-5% ROE against a 13% cost of equity justifies a fraction of book. SBC-zero forward path (fully vested pre-IPO options, H1 FY2026 charge 0.06% of revenue): house and street coincide, band_position is null - the band collapsed, it is not a 0% reading. Historical equity CAGR is IPO- and placing-funded, not retained earnings; EPS CAGR is negative - growth divergence flagged.

equity_bridge.item: Pre-IPO share option exercise proceeds (67.2189m x HK$0.183 / 1.1724)
equity_bridge.note: Options are included in shares_outstanding; proceeds added at exercise. H1 FY2026 interim report share-option note (2473.HK_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:3094)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run base-case revenue growth (base path compounds at ~2.2%/yr over 10 years). The equity CAGR is not usable - it is the Nov 2023 IPO and the 2026 placings, not retained earnings; the EPS/net-income CAGRs are negative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR +20.1% vs EPS 3yr CAGR -27.3% and revenue +17.7%: revenue growth came from a 4.4%-gross-margin export/outright-sales segment (22% of FY2025 revenue) while pre-tax margin fell from 10.0% (FY2023) to 3.1% (FY2025) and 2.5% (H1 FY2026); equity grew by capital raising. Owner FCF is negative in every year (lease book growth in OCF) so no FCF CAGR is computable - FY2022..FY2025 owner FCF -223 / -165 / -341 / -534 RMB m; H1 FY2026 +120 as the book shrank 3.4%.
historical_growth.notes: History FY2021-FY2025 (5 annual periods), so 4-year is the longest CAGR available. Revenue 1,171 -> 1,142 -> 1,304 -> 1,464 -> 1,862 RMB m; net income 34.1 (attrib) / 77.1 / 109.8 / 39.7 / 45.8; equity 443.5 / 506.6 / 781.5 / 827.8 / 877.9 (1,130.7 at H1 FY2026 after RMB ~253m of placings).

base.ebitda_margin_note: Post-finance-cost EBITDA = pre-tax margin + da_pct + sbc_pct. Pre-tax margin path 2.2 / 2.6 / 3.0 / 3.4 / 3.7 / 4.0 flat: FY2026 troughs below FY2025's 3.1% (H1 FY2026 2.5%, NI -22.7%), recovers as weighted funding cost keeps falling (-1.1pp YoY in H1 FY2026), outlet count stabilises at ~111 and opex stops outrunning gross profit; never regains FY2023's 10% because the OEM-captive squeeze on finance-lease yields is structural. Implies ROE ~5% by year 6.
base.capex_note: Maintenance only: fleet renewal = D&A (10.5%) + office-lease principal (0.4%). Fleet and receivable growth are charged through wc_capture_pct.
base.cash_tax_note: PRC statutory 25%; effective FY2024 25.5%, FY2025 21.6%, cash tax paid FY2025 RMB 16.1m on PBT 58.5m (27.6%).
base.wc_note: Equity-funded share of net-operating-asset growth at constant 65.7% gearing: equity/revenue 0.61. Negative = growth consumes equity; revenue decline releases it.
base.sbc_note: SBC-zero forward path: pre-IPO options are fully vested (charge RMB 3.9m FY2025, 0.4m H1 FY2026 = 0.06% of revenue) and no new scheme grants are disclosed; row kept explicit at 0% per house rule, so house and street coincide and band_position is null.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin 2.5 / 3.5 / 4.5 / 5.5 / 6.3 / 7.0 flat: domestic demand normalises from FY2027 as anti-price-war guidance takes hold, NEV-mix and Central-Asia export scale restore operating leverage, funding cost falls another 1-2pp. Still below FY2023's 10%. Implies ROE ~8-9%.
bull.wc_note: Lighter than base (-50 vs -60): incremental revenue skews to asset-light export/outright sales and rental tie-ups that need less book per RMB of revenue.
bull.sbc_note: SBC-zero forward path: pre-IPO options are fully vested (charge RMB 3.9m FY2025, 0.4m H1 FY2026 = 0.06% of revenue) and no new scheme grants are disclosed; row kept explicit at 0% per house rule, so house and street coincide and band_position is null.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Pre-tax margin 1.5 / 1.2 / 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.5 flat: OEM-captive zero-rate financing keeps taking the core finance-lease customer (core revenue already -13% in H1 FY2026), lower-tier-city demand stays weak after the purchase-tax step-up, used-car residuals fall and impairment rises from the 1.0% allowance, e-hailing dual-licence compliance strands part of the fleet. ROE ~1-2%.
bear.wc_note: Half of the base rate: the book runs off and would release ~60% of lost revenue as equity at constant gearing, but there is no dividend policy and a controller who redeploys - only about half of the released capital is credited to shareholders (via deleveraging that accrues to equity); the rest is absorbed by elevated repossession losses and sub-economic redeployment into exports and smart-mobility ventures. Growth is zero from year 5 so the terminal year carries no run-off release.
bear.sbc_note: SBC-zero forward path: pre-IPO options are fully vested (charge RMB 3.9m FY2025, 0.4m H1 FY2026 = 0.06% of revenue) and no new scheme grants are disclosed; row kept explicit at 0% per house rule, so house and street coincide and band_position is null.

scenario_narratives.base: The core domestic finance-lease book stops shrinking but does not regain its FY2023 economics: revenue dips ~2% in FY2026 (H1 -1%, H2 weaker) and is flat in FY2027 as OEM captives keep subsidising zero-rate loans, then grows 3-4% as the NEV mix (32.7% of H1 FY2026 new-car sales), the Hello Car Rental co-branded stores and the Central-Asia export subsidiaries scale. Pre-tax margin troughs at 2.2% and rebuilds to 4% by FY2031 on lower weighted funding cost and a stabilised 111-outlet network. ROE peaks around 5% - below the 13% cost of equity - so every RMB of book growth is reinvested at a loss to shareholders, which is why the base value sits well below book. No dividend; capital stays in the business.
scenario_narratives.bull: Domestic passenger-vehicle demand normalises from FY2027 as the PRC anti-price-war guidance and trade-in support take hold, lower-tier-city customers return to finance leases, and the export arm (revenue +571% in FY2025) becomes an authorised first-tier dealer in Central Asia at scale. Revenue compounds 5-8% for four years, operating leverage on a fixed outlet base plus another 1-2pp of funding-cost reduction lift the pre-tax margin to 7% by FY2031 (ROE ~8-9%), and incremental growth is asset-light (wc capture -50). Even here ROE stays below the cost of equity, so the bull value is roughly half of book - the re-rating thesis is the market paying up for a 7% ROE lender.
scenario_narratives.bear: The OEM-captive squeeze that cut core finance-lease revenue 13% in H1 FY2026 continues: revenue falls 10%, 8%, 5%, 2% then flat; pre-tax margin sinks to 1.0-1.5% as used-car residuals weaken, impairment rises from the 1.0% allowance ratio, and e-hailing dual-licence rules strand fleet vehicles. The book runs off at constant gearing but the controller (Mr Huang, who sold shares into both 2026 top-up placings and re-subscribed at HK$0.98 and HK$0.82) redeploys the released capital into exports and smart-mobility rather than returning it, so shareholders see only half of it. Further top-up placings at distressed prices and a rollover squeeze on RMB 1.27bn of current borrowings are the tail risks this case does not fully price.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 35%: the structural threat (OEM-subsidised financing displacing independent lessors) is already visible in reported numbers (core revenue -13%, NI -23% in H1 FY2026), the balance sheet rolls RMB 1.27bn of secured current borrowings, and the controller has shown he will issue equity at distressed prices. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things at once - a domestic demand recovery, export execution outside China, and continued funding-cost declines - and even then ROE stays below the cost of equity. Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value what the equity actually receives: a levered finance-lease lender is worth the present value of its free cash flow to equity at its own cost of equity, with borrowings treated as operating funding rather than net debt. On that basis XXF earns 3-5% on a RMB 1.13bn equity base against a 13% RMB cost of equity, so it is worth a fraction of book regardless of the optical P/B of ~0.46x. Book value (HK$0.69/share) is a liquidation reference, not a floor, because the controlling shareholder is growing the book, not running it off, and because reinvestment below the cost of equity destroys value each year. The valuation is deliberately not a price-momentum call on a stock that has fallen 97% from its January 2026 high.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: at 13% with a 10x FCFE cap the terminal value is modest; every 1pp of CoE moves the base value ~10-15%. A reader who believes 11% is right for a HK-listed Chinese small-cap lender gets a value ~25% higher - still below the price.

ROE recovery: the base assumes pre-tax margin rebuilds from 2.2% to 4.0%; if FY2023's 10% were ever regained the stock would be worth well above the price. That requires the OEM-captive competition to abate, which nothing in the H1 FY2026 report suggests.

Growth charge (wc_capture): -60 assumes constant gearing. If the lender levers further (gearing was 73.4% before the placings) growth consumes less equity near term but adds refinancing risk; if it delevers, more.
Credit quality: the 1.0% allowance on RMB 1.84bn of receivables and <1% over-3-month past-due are self-reported; a 3pp loss rate would wipe out two years of earnings.

Dilution: two controller-led top-up placings in 2026 added 20% to the count at HK$0.98 and HK$0.82. A further placing near HK$0.3 would be heavily dilutive to per-share value; it is not in the share path.

Price regime: the February 2026 collapse from HK$13.8 to HK$2.0 on 2.4bn shares in a week is a liquidity/holding-structure event, not a fundamental one; the quote may continue to be driven by forced selling rather than value.
